appraisal_events.evidence: "j'ai compris que...il avait voulu se rendre compte par ses questions si la mémoire de ma grand'mère était bien intacte"; "regardant ma grand'mère d'un œil lucide, librement et comme enfin sur la terre ferme"; "Vous irez bien, Madame...où vous aurez repris la vie commune."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator retrospectively credits du Boulbon's literary chat as a skillful diagnostic maneuver, and describes him decisively pushing aside hesitation and possible objections to deliver a confident, penetrating verdict, casting him as authoritative and discerning.

status_effects.explanation: He speaks with marked authority and discernment, decisively overriding lingering doubt and the family's unspoken objections to take full command of the exchange.
She is the object of a gentle, confident reassurance ('vous irez bien...vous n'avez rien'), even though this occurs within a covert test of her memory and mental state.

ambiguities: Du Boulbon's confident reassurance to la grand-mère ('vous n'avez rien') could read ironically in light of the wider narrative, but within this local passage it is presented as sincere and kind, so the positive local reading is preferred rather than being recast as diminishment.
